newsitem.title: UK: UK's large users call for review of electricity Pool.
newsitem.headline: UK's large users call for review of electricity Pool.

text.p: The UK's Energy Intensive Users Group (EIUG), which combines trade associations in some of the most energy intensive industries in the country, has called for a full review of the electricity Pool by the incoming Labour government.

Ian Blakey, chairman of the EIUG, has written to John Battle, Minister of State at the Department of Trade and Industry and former opposition energy spokesman, asking him to review the Pool, the current system under which price competition operates. The EIUG claims that the Pool works in the interests of suppliers but not consumers.

Under the pool, generators bid to supply electricity on a half-hour by half-hour basis 24 hours in advance, and the National Grid Company (NGC) accepts such bids as it needs to fulfill demand in that half hour, using the price of the last bid accepted as the benchmark at which all suppliers are paid.

But the EIUG complains that this is in effect a legalised cartel, in which there is no bulk electricity price available to large users, and no chance for large customers to contract directly with suppliers without going through the pool - all of whose members are suppliers. It is also the only market where all suppliers are paid the same price, regardless of the cost of production.
Blakey said on Tuesday that a review is needed urgently.

"We very much hope that a review of the Pool will be undertaken as a matter of urgency. The electricity industry has come a long way since privatisation, but there needs to be real change if the market is to benefit all customers rather than the suppliers."
Lisa Waters of the EIUG added that the group is so far only calling for a review, without having a firm view of what conclusions it should reach.
"The industry needs one year to come up with a plan and one year to implement it, but it's now seven years since privatisation and we urgently need a review," she said.
She added that the gas industry under competition had seen a more hands on regulator in Ofgas than electricity has experienced with regulator Offer, led by Stephen Littlechild.
"Littlechild has taken a far more hands off approach. We hope Labour will take a far more hands on approach. Competition is about customers," she said.

Since the introduction of competition, she said, gas prices have fallen by around 15 percent while electricity prices have risen by 2 percent, but she added that John Battle has been "saying the right things" about competition in the Pool while in opposition.
